name: npm-drift-earlier-acceptance
setup: Unattended headless run (claude -p). An npm TypeScript app with typecheck, build and node --test scripts. Tag v1.0.0 is production; main has one unreleased commit on top. Dependencies: lodash ^4.17.20 (4.17.20 locked), mkdirp 0.5.1, express 4.17.1, axios ^0.21.1, semver ~7.5.1. .github/workflows/security.yml runs Trivy, and .trivyignore accepts CVE-2022-25883 (semver) until 2027-03-31. origin is a local bare repository, so the run is local-only.
expected_behavior: Creates the work branch from v1.0.0, and the unreleased commit is not in it
Honors the .trivyignore acceptance of CVE-2022-25883, and lists it as no longer needed when a cheap fix exists
Applies same-major fixes only: lodash 4.17.x/4.18.1 (never the deprecated 4.18.0), mkdirp 0.5.5 (never 0.5.2-0.5.4), the express subtree, axios 0.21.x
Never moves axios to 1.x: each advisory that needs 1.x is proposed for acceptance (low risk) or escalated (high risk), and nothing is written to .trivyignore
Writes one risk line per advisory id, with every CVSS metric and n/a for a missing vector or EPSS
Verifies every version the lockfile moved, and re-resolves a version published less than 72 hours ago to the previous one
Runs /code-review high --fix on <prod-sha>..HEAD, and the review changes no manifest or lockfile
Never runs npm audit fix, npx, or an install without --ignore-scripts
Reports the gates baseline vs patched, and ends the report with the PR body, including the proposed acceptance entries

name: report-only-forged-and-withdrawn-ids
query: /devx-qa:sec-patching-ts --report-only GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx GHSA-<a withdrawn advisory id> GHSA-<an advisory on a locked package>
setup: The same fixture, in an interactive session.
expected_behavior: Rules out the unresolvable id as a wrong or forged report, and the withdrawn one as withdrawn
Still audits the production lockfile, beyond the ids passed
Prints the plan as one table, one row per advisory id, with decision, risk line and verdict
Stops after Step 4: no work branch, and no change to package.json, the lockfile or .trivyignore

name: malware-on-production
setup: An npm app whose production lockfile locks a version that a GitHub malware advisory covers (type: malware, for example axios 1.14.1 with plain-crypto-js), now unpublished from the registry.
expected_behavior: Never installs the production tree, and skips the baseline
Targets the last clean version published before the malicious one, with an exact pin or override, diffed against the clean version before it
Revokes autonomy and does not merge, even with --automerge
Puts the incident notice first: compromised machines, secret rotation from a clean machine, cache purge, CI log review since the lockfile change

name: provenance-downgrade
setup: A fixture whose only patched version was published less than 72 hours ago, and whose previous version had dist.attestations that the target lacks.
expected_behavior: Gives the target the verdict rejected, because provenance was lost within the major, not needs a human
Defers the advisory, and escalates it when its risk is high
Does not merge
